how_to_read: 1. Read the head first: the first 33 lines hold manifest, essence and routing (Read limit=33, or jq '{manifest, essence, routing}' shop-component.metadump.json).
2. Pick the route for your job and run its jq: jq '<routing[i].jq>' shop-component.metadump.json

ladder: product cards, carts and quick add
a compact, minimal, modern shopping component

essence.one_sentence: A compact, minimal, modern shopping component: by default one product card in a grid (a near-square picture, the name, an optional meta line, the price and a labelled add control) whose confirmation stays on screen long enough to read; the placement of the add control and the other parts are options.

poles: tiles about 140 to 148 px wide, four across a 640 px frame with 16 px gutters
every part named: the name, the price and an add label that says what it does
hairline borders, one accent, no decoration
feedback that stays readable after the tap

readings.reading: buy box on a product page

routing.when: pull first for any job: the most relevant entries (relevance, not rules)
choosing parts, their order, layout and reading
choosing spacing, type, color roles, radius, borders and dark mode
specifying hover, focus, pressed, disabled, loading, added, error, timing and reduced motion
reviewing a rendered output or a draft against the dump

ak-component-hardware.excluded_sense: hardware or electronic part, such as a resistor, a chip or a PC part
ak-component-hardware.instead: UI component: a reusable interface unit with states, such as a product card

ak-minimal-empty.excluded_sense: empty or unfinished: missing parts a shopper needs
ak-minimal-empty.instead: the fewest elements that still work, each one finished

ak-gray-on-gray.instead: text at 4.5:1 or higher against its background (3:1 for large text and UI boundaries), taken from a secondary-text role token that still passes
ak-gray-on-gray.text: No faint gray text that fails contrast.

ak-noise-stunning.text: Empty intensifier. It names no property or value; describe the surface, spacing or motion instead.

ak-noise-seamless.text: Empty intensifier. It names no property or value; say what the transition does instead.

ak-compact-dense.excluded_sense: information-dense: many data points packed into one view
ak-compact-dense.instead: small footprint: few parts and short distances, with ordered spacing
ak-compact-dense.text: Default card reading only: 'compact' means a small footprint, not a dense tile with many data points. A dense reading stays one option among others.

ak-glass-card.instead: a flat surface: a solid background token with a hairline border or none, and the radius from the radius token
ak-glass-card.text: Default product card only: no frosted, blurred or translucent card surface. A glass surface stays one option among others for the card's look.
ak-glass-card.trigger: a default reach for a modern look

ak-gradient-button.instead: a solid fill from the single action color token, with a text label and a visible focus ring
ak-gradient-button.text: Default product card only: no gradient fill on the add control. A gradient stays one option among others.

ak-hover-lift.instead: hover changes the border or background by one step of the surface tokens, with no scale, translate or shadow change
ak-hover-lift.text: Default product card only: no lift, zoom or drop shadow on hover. A hover lift stays one option among others.

ak-countdown.instead: no timer; a real end date in plain text only when the product data carries one
ak-countdown.text: Default product card only: no countdown or ticking deal timer on the card. Other readings may show a real end date in plain text when the product data carries one.

ak-scarcity-banner.instead: a plain stock line in the meta text style, shown only when the stock count is real and low
ak-scarcity-banner.text: Default product card only: no alarm banner or urgency copy; a plain stock line, when the stock count is real and low, is the default.

ak-badge-stack.instead: at most one status word in the meta line, such as New or Sale, and only when the product data says so
ak-badge-stack.text: Default product card only: no stack of status badges or corner ribbons. At most one status word in the meta line, when the product data says so.

ak-icon-only-add.instead: a visible text label, Add or Add to cart, with an optional icon beside it and an accessible name that matches the label
ak-icon-only-add.text: Default product card only: the add control at rest shows a visible text label (inv-add-label), not only an icon.

ak-pulsing-add.instead: a static control; the added state changes its color or label once, in a short ease-out transition under about 200 ms, then stops
ak-pulsing-add.text: Default product card only: no looping pulse, bounce or shake on the add control. A looping cue stays one option among others.

ak-stock-photo.instead: the product's own image at one fixed aspect ratio, or a neutral tone block with the product name when no image exists
ak-stock-photo.text: Default product card only: no generic stock photo standing in for the product; the product's own image, or a neutral tone block with the product name, is the default.

ak-shopping-hobby.excluded_sense: window shopping or shopping as a leisure hobby
ak-shopping-hobby.instead: the purchase flow: from a product to adding it to the bag
ak-shopping-hobby.text: Default reading only (the purchase flow from a product to the bag): 'shopping' here excludes window shopping. Browsing-led readings stay one option among others.

ak-modern-trendy.excluded_sense: trendy effects such as neon glows or glassmorphism
ak-modern-trendy.instead: current conventions: clear type, honest color, familiar controls and visible states
ak-modern-trendy.text: Default reading only: 'modern' means current conventions, not neon glows or glassmorphism. A trendy look stays one option among others.

ak-trend-effects.instead: a neutral surface, system type and one action color token
ak-trend-effects.text: Default product card only: no neon, glow, aurora or blob effects on the card. A trend effect stays one option among others.

ak-tiny-target.instead: a control at least 24 by 24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 minimum), and 48 by 48 px on touch with 8 px between targets
ak-tiny-target.text: No add, quantity or remove control below the minimum target size: 24 by 24 CSS px at least, and 48 by 48 px on touch with 8 px between targets (44 px is the floor option).

k-compact-footprint.text: Tiles read compact: about 140 to 148 px wide, four across a 640 px frame with 16 px gutters.

test.spec: tile width 140 to 148 px at a 640 px frame with 16 px gutters; four tiles across

k-minimal-parts.text: The default card shows only its listed parts; an optional extra (rating, sale pill, swatches, stock line, stepper) appears only when it earns its place.

test.spec: list the visible parts; each is a default part or an optional extra named in an-parts-optional

k-card-order.text: Parts read top to bottom: picture, name, meta line if shown, price, then the add control.

test.spec: the order of the parts in the rendered tile matches the list

k-no-icon-only-add.text: The add control shows a visible text label at rest and has an accessible name that names the product.

test.spec: the add control has visible text at rest; its accessible name includes the product name

k-feedback-persistent.text: On the default card the added confirmation stays readable; no overlay on it fades out quickly.

test.spec: after add, the confirmation remains visible long enough to read and is not a fast-fading overlay

k-response-limits.text: The pressed state appears within about 0.1 s of the tap; a loading or added state is visible for anything slower than about 1 s.

test.spec: pressed feedback at or under 100 ms; loading or added visible past 1000 ms

k-target-size.text: Pointer targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS px; touch targets are at least 48 by 48 px with 8 px or more between them.

test.spec: computed hit area of the add and stepper controls against 24 px and 48 px on touch

k-text-contrast.text: Text meets 4.5:1 against its surface, and large text meets 3:1.

test.spec: ratio of every text colour against its surface colour

k-accessible-names.text: Each add button names its product; each picture has a text alternative; each tile heading is level three.

test.spec: read the accessibility tree: button names include the product name

k-state-not-color-alone.text: Every state change carries a second cue beside colour: shape, text, icon or size.

test.spec: remove colour from the rendered states; each state still reads

k-no-hover-lift.text: On the default card, no lift, zoom or drop shadow on hover.

test.spec: no transform, scale or box-shadow added in :hover on the card

k-no-countdown.text: On the default card, no countdown or ticking deal timer.

test.spec: no timer element or ticking text on the default card

q-framework.text: Which front-end stack will the component be built in?
q-framework.default: framework-agnostic markup and CSS tokens; a React example is acceptable

q-reading.text: Which shopping component: product card, mini cart, product list, checkout summary, or buy box?

q-apple-44.text: Is Apple's 44 pt default target confirmed on Apple's own page?
q-apple-44.default: Treat 44 pt as the comfortable size and 24 CSS px as the WCAG floor.
q-apple-44.impact: target sizes on a compact card
q-apple-44.resolve: Apple layout and accessibility pages did not render this session

q-low-stock-n.text: At what remaining stock count does a low-stock notice appear?
q-low-stock-n.default: no notice until the product is out of stock
q-low-stock-n.resolve: ask the merchant or the user

q-confirm-ms.text: How long should an add confirmation stay on screen when the shopper does not touch the card again, in ms?
q-confirm-ms.default: until the shopper's next action, with no timer (the persistent confirmation of the default card); a timed option of about 3000 to 5000 ms is to be tested (opt-feedback-duration b)
q-confirm-ms.impact: whether the confirmation can be read in time
q-confirm-ms.resolve: test with users; no fetched source gives a value

q-motion-ms.text: How long should hover, press and reveal transitions run, in ms?
q-motion-ms.default: 80 to 100 ms with ease-out, so pressed and hover feedback stay at or under the 100 ms response limit (opt-motion-durations)
q-motion-ms.impact: perceived response of the add control
q-motion-ms.resolve: check against the NN/g 0.1 s limit on a real device

q-reduced-motion.text: How should reduced-motion users see the reveal and the count change?
q-reduced-motion.default: remove the movement; keep the colour, text and count change (prefers-reduced-motion)
q-reduced-motion.impact: motion sensitivity, and whether the state change is still visible
q-reduced-motion.resolve: no fetched source covers the rule; test with reduced motion on

q-error-presentation.text: How is a failed add presented?
q-error-presentation.default: an inline text message beside the control, with the label back to Add, and the same text in the polite status region so it is announced (opt-error-presentation a and b)
q-error-presentation.resolve: no fetched source covers the error state; choose and test

q-disabled-semantics.text: Should a disabled add control use the disabled attribute or aria-disabled?
q-disabled-semantics.default: aria-disabled, so the control stays focusable, with the reason in text beside it (st-disabled, cp-disabled-state)
q-disabled-semantics.impact: keyboard focus and what a screen reader announces
q-disabled-semantics.resolve: test with screen-reader users; the sources do not settle it

q-add-label.text: Which add label wording: Add to bag, Add to cart or Add?
q-add-label.default: Add to bag (the moodboard wording), with the product name in the accessible name
q-add-label.impact: recognition and the label's length on a narrow tile
q-add-label.resolve: check against the shop's own vocabulary

q-quantity-ceiling.text: What is the largest quantity a stepper accepts?
q-quantity-ceiling.default: no fixed ceiling in the component; stop at the known stock count when the product data carries one. The nine-piece limit is a demo choice, not a rule.
q-quantity-ceiling.impact: the stepper's limit message and focus
q-quantity-ceiling.resolve: set from the shop's stock and order rules

p-make.anchor: make a compact, minimal, modern shopping component

p-compact.text: The component is compact. What compact means here is open: see senses and readings.

ux_principles._about: Discipline primer for the rung UX and UI design: named laws, heuristics and standards that apply to a compact, minimal shopping component. Laws and heuristics are researched from fetched pages; applications to this task are labeled inferred in the text.

p-fitts-law.text: Fitts's law: the time to acquire a target is a function of the distance to and size of the target. Applied here: the add control and the card's clickable area need enough size and a short distance from the cursor path.

good: a full-width add button on a compact card
bad: a tiny text link as the only add control

p-hick-law.text: Hick's law: the time it takes to make a decision increases with the number and complexity of choices. Applied here: each visible option on a card (size, color, quantity) adds decision time, so variant choices belong behind one selector.

good: one variant selector that opens a list
bad: five unlabeled swatches and three steppers on every card

p-jakob-law.text: Jakob's law: users prefer your site to work the same way as all the other sites they already know. Applied here: the add control, price placement and cart badge should follow shopping conventions a shopper already knows, so the modern look does not cost recognition.

good: price under the name, add button at the bottom of the card
bad: an unfamiliar gesture as the only way to add

p-proximity.text: Law of proximity (Gestalt): objects that are near, or proximate to each other, tend to be grouped together. Applied here: name, price and meta sit close together as one group, and the add control is separated from the group by space, so the card reads as the product plus one action.

good: price and name grouped, larger gap before the button
bad: equal gaps between every line, so the price reads as a separate item

p-visibility-of-status.text: Visibility of system status (Nielsen heuristic 1): the design should keep users informed about what is going on. Applied here: adding to cart shows a visible state change (pending, added, cart count) so the shopper knows the action landed.

good: button shows Added and the cart count updates

p-recognition-over-recall.text: Recognition rather than recall (Nielsen heuristic 6): minimize the user's memory load by making elements, actions, and options visible. Applied here: the selected variant, quantity and cart state stay on screen rather than being remembered from a previous step.

good: selected size shown on the card
bad: size chosen on a previous screen and not shown

p-contrast-text.text: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), level AA: text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1; large text (roughly 18pt or 14pt bold) needs at least 3:1. Applied here: price, name and meta text, and the add label, meet 4.5:1 against their background; the grey meta text is the usual failure.

good: dark grey meta text on white at 4.5:1 or more
bad: light grey placeholder-weight meta text on white

p-contrast-non-text.text: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, level AA: the visual presentation of the following has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors, including visual information needed to identify a UI component or state. Applied here: a card border, a button edge and a focus ring need 3:1 against the surface they sit on.

good: focus ring at 3:1 or more against the card
bad: a near-white border on a near-white card as the only edge of the add button

p-target-size.term: WCAG 2.2 target size 24 by 24 CSS px
p-target-size.text: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), level AA: the size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, with a spacing exception when a 24 CSS pixel circle around each undersized target does not intersect another target. Applied here: the add, quantity and variant controls are at least 24 by 24 CSS px; a compact card can still meet this with padding around a smaller visual mark.

good: add button 40px tall with full width
bad: a 16px icon-only stepper with no padding

p-common-mistakes.term: common mistakes in compact shopping components
p-common-mistakes.text: Common mistakes (inferred from practice): low-contrast meta text that fails 4.5:1; icon-only add buttons with no label or accessible name; small tap targets packed too closely; price shown without its unit or currency; hover-only reveals of the add control, which fail on touch and keyboard; too many competing accents so the add action is not the clearest choice; crowding a card with ratings, badges and promos so the product name is lost.
p-common-mistakes.never_implies: that a rating or badge is always wrong; they are optional and can be shown when they carry information

commerce_vocabulary._about: Vocabulary for the rung e-commerce interfaces: the parts and actions a shopping component is named by. Inferred from common practice; the terms are how practitioners and shoppers name the parts.

v-product-card.text: Product card: the repeated unit in a product list, usually an image, a name, a price and optionally an add action, linked to the product page.

v-quick-add.text: Quick add: adding a product to the cart directly from a product card or list, without opening the product page. Often paired with a mini cart (a small panel or drawer showing items, quantity and subtotal) that confirms the add.

commerce_patterns._about: Patterns and failure modes for product cards, the add-to-cart control and quick add. Researched entries cite fetched pages; inferred entries are this build's reading of them and are tier 2 at most.

exemplars._about: Illustrative exemplars, labeled as examples, each with what transfers (a relationship) and what does not.

ex-apple-mac.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
ex-apple-mac.text: Exemplar: a category page of about thirty product tiles, each named by its configuration (screen size, chip, memory, storage, color), with no price on the tile and a single 'Shop now' button. Price and purchase sit on the next step.
ex-apple-mac.transfers: The relationship: the variant is chosen on the tile, and price and purchase come on a detail step, so the card carries no price-and-cart conflict.
ex-apple-mac.does_not_transfer: Brand chrome, legal footnotes, the education-store link and the product set itself.

ex-burberry.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
ex-burberry.text: Exemplar of what to avoid: NN/g's review of a fashion retailer's add-to-cart overlay found it showed the addition but disappeared quickly, so shoppers could not check what they had added.
ex-burberry.transfers: The lesson that a confirmation must stay long enough to read and act on.
ex-burberry.does_not_transfer: Anything about that retailer's styling or layout.

ex-dawn.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
ex-dawn.text: Exemplar: Shopify's open-source reference theme describes itself as HTML-first, with JavaScript only as needed; its repository is organized into sections and snippets folders, which is where product and cart components would live.
ex-dawn.transfers: Server-rendered state and progressive enhancement: the card works before script runs, and script adds only what it needs.

cp-live-region.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
cp-live-region.text: Accessible add-to-cart flows announce cart changes through a live region that already exists in the DOM, with aria-live set to polite or assertive, whose text script updates. The speaker's own wording: live regions are a way to announce changes in your site to assistive technology users. Notifications that hold interactive content are better handled by moving focus to them than by a live region alone.

cp-disabled-state.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
cp-disabled-state.text: Setting the disabled attribute on the add button can drop keyboard focus unless focus is managed afterward; aria-disabled keeps it focusable but may be announced as unavailable, which reads ambiguously in shopping. A speaker on accessible add-to-cart flows recommends user testing to choose between them (source: s-nicchan). Forum reports show sold-out states failing when the label, the disabled attribute and the stock check disagree, so these three should agree and survive a variant switch or refresh (s-nicchan and forum snippets, not fetched).

cp-size-buttons.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
cp-size-buttons.text: Baymard's eye-tracking found users were more likely to overlook size selectors presented as drop-down menus, and its guideline title is 'Always Use Buttons for Size Selection'. Implication for a card or buy box (inferred): show the variant choice as visible buttons or swatches rather than a hidden menu, and make the selected state visibly stronger.

cp-competing-cta.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
cp-competing-cta.text: Baymard's add-to-cart prominence guideline says competing call-to-action buttons are distracting and make it needlessly difficult to add a product to the cart. Implication (inferred): a card carries one primary add action, and secondary actions such as wishlist or compare get lower visual weight.

cp-button-label.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
cp-button-label.text: Label states for the add control can run Add to cart, then Adding, then Added to cart, per the accessibility speaker (s-nicchan). The same speaker notes that 'Added to Cart' can read as a link to checkout, so pair the label with a non-text cue such as a count badge. 'Add to bag' and 'add to cart' are both common; 'quick add' names the card-level control, not the product-page buy box. Vocabulary is inferred from search snippets, not fetched pages.

cp-feedback-persistent.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
cp-feedback-persistent.text: Default card: add-to-cart feedback stays readable on screen. NN/g reports that an overlay on one fashion retailer confirmed the addition but disappeared quickly, and advises against disappearing overlays; NN/g also suggests a number badge plus a confirmation popover or page. Baymard describes an 'Added to Cart' overlay as a highly effective confirmation. A timed toast is one option among others (opt-feedback-duration). The sources give no duration in milliseconds; that is an open question.

specifics._about: Measured values, sizes and timings with the source each came from. Values marked inferred are not confirmed against a fetched primary source.

sp-target-wcag.rung: a compact, minimal, modern shopping component
sp-target-wcag.text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.5.8 (level AA): the size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, except under listed exceptions (spacing, equivalent, inline, user agent control, essential). A 24 px square has to fit inside the target, and padding around a smaller icon can supply that hit area.

sp-target-material.rung: a compact, minimal, modern shopping component
sp-target-material.text: Material guidance: consider touch targets at least 48x48 dp, separated by 8 dp of space or more (about 9 mm). An element like an icon may appear to be 24x24 dp while the padding around it makes the full 48x48 dp touch target. Visible size and tap area can differ.

sp-focus-appearance.rung: a compact, minimal, modern shopping component
sp-focus-appearance.text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.4.13 (level AAA): the focus indicator is at least as large as a 2 CSS px perimeter of the unfocused component, and has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 between focused and unfocused states. Use a visible ring that clears 3:1, as a target for the focus-visible state.

sp-response-limits.rung: a compact, minimal, modern shopping component

values.feel: directly manipulating objects in the UI
freely navigating without unduly waiting for the computer
about the limit for keeping the user's attention focused on the dialogue

sp-response-limits.text: NN/g's response time limits: about 0.1 s feels like directly manipulating objects, about 1 s lets the user move freely without waiting, and about 10 s is the limit for holding attention. Use them to decide the feedback for a tap: a pressed state within about 0.1 s, a visible loading or added state for anything slower than about 1 s.

sp-price-del.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
sp-price-del.note: Implication (inferred): mark the former price with del so the meaning survives outside styling, and keep the current price as the dominant one.
sp-price-del.text: MDN: the del element represents a range of text that has been deleted from a document, and is often, but need not be, rendered with a strike-through style. A former price marked with del carries its meaning in the markup, not only in the styling.

sp-price-sale-rule.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
sp-price-sale-rule.text: Sale display (inferred from practitioner summaries that were not fetched): show the current price as the most prominent price, with the former price smaller and crossed out, and only when the former price is real. Keep the sale display consistent from card to cart, because a shopper who sees the sale vanish at checkout doubts the discount.

sp-target-44-inferred.rung: a compact, minimal, modern shopping component
sp-target-44-inferred.text: Apple's guidance is commonly cited as a default target of 44x44 pt for iOS controls, and WCAG 2.5.5 (level AAA) as 44x44 CSS px. Weakness: the Apple layout and accessibility pages did not render, and both figures come from secondary summaries only. Check Apple's page before quoting it (q-apple-44). Recommendation for touch: 48 px (sp-target-material); 44 px is the floor option; 24 px is the WCAG floor.

compact_card._about: Structure, layout, add-control states and feedback of one compact product card block, read from a scraped product page and its preview screenshot. Quoted and paraphrased facts are the page's; the transfer notes are ours.

options._about: options, not requirements: layouts that trade columns for tile width

opt-three-across.text: Option: three tiles across a 640 px frame, each about 200 px wide (3 x 200 + 2 x 16 = 632 px). Wider tiles belong to fewer columns, so the column count follows from the tile width. One option among others.

How does the quantity stepper work?

cc-stepper-limit-focus.text: The plus stops at nine in this demo, and the control says so when the limit is reached. When minus removes the last piece, focus returns to the single plus, so a keyboard user keeps their place. The bag total in the heading row is the sum of every count, which makes the stepper's numbers visible at the group level.
cc-stepper-limit-focus.quote: Minus at one removes the piece, and focus moves back to the plus so a keyboard user keeps their place.

cc-visual-frame.term: preview look: hairline frame and greyscale tiles

heading_path: Compact Product Card Block for React

cc-visual-frame.text: In the preview screenshot the block sits on a dark page as a hairline-framed panel with small crosshair marks at its corners. The heading row has the group name on the left and a small count with the bag total on the right, reading 'Showing 8 of 8 · Bag: 0'. Two tiles per row show flat grey picture placeholders above their names and prices. Transfer: hairlines and corner marks give structure without filled backgrounds, and greyscale placeholders keep a dense grid quiet while pictures load.

cc-accessibility-names.term: accessible names on the add control

heading_path: Compact Product Card Block for React

cc-accessibility-names.text: Each picture is a named image, each tile has a level-three heading, and each button names its product, for example 'Add [product] to the bag' or 'One fewer [product]'. The count is announced by the polite status line, and everything works from the keyboard. Reduced motion removes the reveal transition.
cc-accessibility-names.quote: Each picture is a named image, each tile has an h3, and the buttons name the product

heading_path: Compact Product Card Block for React

cc-parts-order.text: Placement option B from the compact demo: a hairline frame with a plus mark at each corner; a heading row with the group name and a count; a grid of tiles set between shared hairlines. Inside each tile: a greyscale picture with a round plus in its corner, then the name as a heading, then the price. The demo's round plus has no visible label at rest, so under inv-add-label it needs one (anatomy/options/add_placement). The whole tile is one link.

heading_path: Compact Product Card Block for React

cc-add-steps.text: Stepper option from the compact demo: after the first add, the add control grows into a pill with minus, the count and plus. Minus at one takes the piece back and the control returns to its labelled rest state. The count shows the piece's quantity in the bag, so the stepper replaces the add control instead of opening a panel. The default card carries no stepper (an-parts-optional).
cc-add-steps.quote: The first press adds one and the button grows into a pill with minus, the count and plus

cc-feedback-status.term: bag count and polite status line

heading_path: Compact Product Card Block for React

cc-feedback-status.text: Default card reading: feedback is local state. The heading row's bag count adds up every piece, and a polite status line announces what changed. Nothing is stored, charged or sent, and motion is limited to CSS for the reveal and the entrance. A card wired to a real add request (a pending state, a persisted cart) is one option among others (states/states/options). A compact card can keep its running total in the heading row and announce changes through a status region instead of a modal.
cc-feedback-status.quote: adds up the pieces and a polite status line says what changed

heading_path: Compact Product Card Block for React
Why is the whole tile a link?

cc-tile-link.text: Default tile reading: the name is the link, and its hit area stretches over the whole tile, so the entire tile works as one target. Where the add control sits on the picture corner (option B), it sits above that area, so pressing it adds to the bag instead of following the link. Where a tile has no room for a separate view button, the tile carries the navigation; a separate view button is an option where the tile has room.
cc-tile-link.quote: the corner button sits above it, so pressing it adds to the bag instead of following the link

cc-grid-layout.term: tile grid and quick add on the card

heading_path: Compact Product Card Block for React

cc-grid-layout.text: Default card reading: eight tiles in a grid, two across on a phone and four across from the small breakpoint (the breakpoint in px is not set; fewer columns with wider tiles is opt-three-across). The card carries its own add control, so a shopper can add without opening a product page; a card whose add lives on the product page is one option (dp-quick-add-vs-buybox). The page names small-goods shelves, search results and dense product lists as the fit.
cc-grid-layout.quote: two across on a phone and four from the small breakpoint

product_card_composition._about: How a product card is composed in a design system: parts, order, purposes and principles. Researched entries are read from one fetched Telerik Design System Kit page; the visual entries are this build's reading of its screenshot.

pc-parts.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
pc-parts.text: The page lists the usual parts of a product card as name, images, price, size, color, brief description, add-to-cart and favorites buttons, and quick preview or compare buttons. It notes that the exact set depends on the product. The card is a compact overview of a product's most significant characteristic, used in a list or grid.

pc-purposes.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
pc-purposes.text: The page gives the card three jobs: it is a navigational element that usually leads to the product page, a compact overview for quick comparison, and a place for actions such as save, add to cart and compare. The whole card is a link target, and the actions sit on it as secondary controls.

pc-principles.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
pc-principles.text: Four principles: simplicity (only the most important details, kept compact), short texts with a character limit on the label and description, image quality with a separate image for every color variation, and consistency (equal card size, similar details, the same internal layout). The consistency rule matters most for grids of mixed products.

pc-image-first-layout.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
pc-image-first-layout.text: Both demo variants put the image at the top of a vertical card, with text and price stacked below it. Product Card 1 has a small image with a sale badge above a name, a color row and a price. Product Card 4 has a tall portrait image with a small badge and a fuller text block. The page does not describe the layout in words; this reading is from the screenshot.

pc-info-order-visual.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
pc-info-order-visual.text: Under the image the order is name, then a secondary line, then price. Card 1 shows a color swatch row with a '+3 more' count on the line under the name. Card 4 adds an address line, a row of small spec icons (area, beds, baths), a price with a struck-through original next to the sale price, and a seller avatar with a date. Price sits on the bottom row in both.

pc-minimal-transfer.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
pc-minimal-transfer.text: For a compact, minimal, modern shopping card, what transfers is the stack: image first, then name, a single price line, and at most one or two secondary details such as a colour count or a sale marker. The page's own cards carry more detail than a minimal card needs, so the transfer is the order and the rules, not the amount of content. Spacing, sizes and type are not given on the page and are set elsewhere.

button_states._about: What each button state must communicate, the sizes the page states, and what transfers to an add-to-cart control. Researched entries are read from one fetched UXPin design guide (a vendor blog page, so its advice is one designer's standard, not a spec). The transfer entry is this build's inference.

aliases: default hover active focus disabled loading toggle
bs-state-set.rung: product cards, carts and quick add

heading_path: Button States Explained: The Complete Design Guide for 2026

bs-state-set.text: The page lists seven standard states: default, hover, active (pressed), focus, disabled, loading and toggle. It says most buttons need four to seven, depending on the product. For a shop add-to-cart control the set that matters is default, hover, pressed, focus-visible, disabled and loading; toggle applies only if the control switches between two conditions such as added and not added.

bs-minimum-set.rung: product cards, carts and quick add

heading_path: Button States Explained: The Complete Design Guide for 2026

bs-minimum-set.text: The FAQ sets a floor of four states: default, hover, active and disabled. It adds focus for keyboard use, and loading and toggle for buttons that run async actions or switch state. Read against a single add-to-cart control, the floor holds, and loading must be added because adding to cart is usually an async request.

bs-hover.rung: product cards, carts and quick add

heading_path: Button States Explained: The Complete Design Guide for 2026

bs-hover.text: Hover signals that the control is clickable. The page advises a subtle change (a slight color shift, an elevation shadow or an underline), kept noticeable but not jarring, with no dramatic animation. Hover does not exist on touch devices, so hover must never be the only place essential information appears, such as the added confirmation.

bs-pressed.rung: product cards, carts and quick add

heading_path: Button States Explained: The Complete Design Guide for 2026

bs-pressed.text: Pressed confirms the system registered the action, between mousedown and mouseup. The page suggests darkening, an inset shadow or a small scale reduction, kept brief and immediate, and reversed cleanly on release. It gives no duration. For add-to-cart, the pressed state is the first acknowledgement, before any request or cart update returns.

bs-focus-ring.rung: product cards, carts and quick add

heading_path: Button States Explained: The Complete Design Guide for 2026

bs-focus-ring.text: Focus shows keyboard position, usually as an outline ring. The page says never remove it, and if the browser outline does not fit, replace it with a custom ring, for example 2 pixels with an offset in the brand color. The ring needs at least 3 to 1 contrast against the background. The page gives no width beyond that example.

bs-disabled-explain.rung: product cards, carts and quick add

heading_path: Button States Explained: The Complete Design Guide for 2026

bs-disabled-explain.text: Disabled says the control is unavailable while it stays visible. The page advises reduced opacity or a muted palette, aria-disabled for screen readers, and where possible a nearby explanation of why it is disabled. For add-to-cart, that means an out-of-stock or unselected-option state should say why in text next to the control, not only grey it out.

bs-loading-lock.rung: product cards, carts and quick add

heading_path: Button States Explained: The Complete Design Guide for 2026

bs-loading-lock.text: Loading shows the action is being processed and prevents double submission. The page suggests swapping the label for a spinner or adding one beside the text, disabling the control while it runs, and showing progress for long operations. A quick add-to-cart request is short, so a spinner with the label kept in place is enough; no percentage is needed.

bs-not-color-alone.term: state not conveyed by color alone
bs-not-color-alone.rung: product cards, carts and quick add

heading_path: Button States Explained: The Complete Design Guide for 2026

bs-not-color-alone.text: The page requires a second cue beside any color change, such as shape, text, icon or size, and states that text on buttons must meet 4.5 to 1 contrast in every state, not only the default. For an added-to-cart state, the change needs a checkmark or label as well as a color, and the text must still pass 4.5 to 1 when the button is pressed or disabled.

bs-add-transfer.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
bs-add-transfer.text: Inferred for the compact card: what transfers is the rule set, not the visual styling. Keep default, hover, pressed, focus ring, disabled-with-reason and, where an add request is pending, a short loading state. Keep the tap target at least 48 by 48 px on touch with 8 px between targets, keep the focus ring visible, and make the added confirmation use text and an icon, not colour or hover alone. The page gives no sizes for the card or spacing around the control.

bs-min-tap-size.rung: product cards, carts and quick add

heading_path: Button States Explained: The Complete Design Guide for 2026

bs-min-tap-size.text: The page gives one size: the default button should be tappable on mobile, at a minimum of 44 by 44 pixels. It gives no desktop size and no size for the focus ring. The source's 44 by 44 px is the floor here; the recommendation for the add control on touch is 48 px (st-default), which a compact card can keep by padding the control rather than enlarging its label.

look_and_feel._about: What the collected images show, seen by eye and sampled by pixel. Exemplars are illustrative, not requirements; palettes are photo samples of screenshots.

tokens._about: Measured or inferred token values for a compact, minimal, modern shopping component. Dark-mode values are photo samples from the moodboard; every other value is an inferred tier-2 starting point with a range, not a brand spec. Contrast ratios are WCAG 2.x relative-luminance ratios computed from the hex pairs written in each text.

lf-spacing-scale.text: Spacing steps of 4, 8, 12, 16, 24 and 32 px. The card uses 12 to 16 px inside its edge, 4 to 8 px between name, meta and price, and 12 to 16 px before the add row, so the gap before the action is larger than the gaps inside the product group (proximity, Gestalt law, in 20-research-primer).

lf-type-price.text: Price at 18 px, weight 600, line height 1.2, with tabular numerals so prices align down a grid. It is larger and heavier than the name (18 px against 15 px, 600 against 500), which matches the moodboard's price-rhythm reading.

lf-color-text.text: Primary text #1A1A1A on the white card surface #FFFFFF gives 17.40:1; on the hover surface #F5F5F5 it gives 15.96:1. Both clear WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 (4.5:1 for normal text). The page background may be #FFFFFF or a shade of it; the card does not need a fill to separate it from the page, the hairline does that job.

lf-image-aspect.text: The three compact exemplar tiles show a roughly square picture filling the tile width (1:1, read by eye, not measured). A 4:5 portrait crop is the common alternative for apparel; the range is wider than the exemplars because the moodboard showed only square crops for these goods. Crop with object-fit cover so every tile keeps one height.

lf-dark-roles.text: Dark roles on the sampled field #0F0F0D and panel #1A1A1A. Primary text #FAFAFA gives 18.38:1 on the field and 16.67:1 on the panel. Muted text #A3A59E (inferred, not sampled) gives 7.71:1 on the field and 6.99:1 on the panel. The control edge #7A7C74 (inferred) gives 4.53:1 on the field and 4.11:1 on the panel, which meets 3:1. The dark hairline #2B2C28 gives 1.36:1, so it is decorative only. The primary button inverts to a #FAFAFA fill with a #0F0F0D label, 18.38:1. The accent #7AA2FF gives 7.71:1 on the field. The photo samples are of screenshots, not brand specifications.
never_implies: a light page with a dark card

lf-color-accent.range: accent any hue at 6:1 or more with white
lf-color-accent.text: Default card reading only: one accent #1F4FD1 used for the action and the focus ring. On the add control the accent is the fill (filled option) or the label and edge (outlined option), see dp-accent-fill. White label on the accent gives 6.78:1 (passes 4.5:1 for normal text). The accent as text on #FFFFFF gives 6.78:1, and on #F5F5F5 gives 6.22:1. The focus ring at 6.78:1 against white clears the 3:1 focus minimum. Other readings may choose another accent or none.

lf-color-old-price.text: A struck-through former price is still text, so it needs 4.5:1. Use #5C6470 on every surface: 5.98:1 on #FFFFFF and 5.48:1 on the #F5F5F5 hover surface, the same grey as the meta text, so one muted role serves both. #6B7280 is 4.83:1 on white but 4.43:1 on #F5F5F5, which fails, so it is not used for the old price. A faded #9AA3B0 gives 2.55:1 and fails. The strike-through line carries the 'was' meaning in the markup (MDN del), so the colour can stay at the passing grey.

lf-color-muted.text: Muted text #5C6470 gives 5.98:1 on #FFFFFF and 5.48:1 on #F5F5F5, so meta text and the old price pass 4.5:1 on both surfaces. The lighter grey #6B7280 gives 4.83:1 on white but only 4.43:1 on #F5F5F5, which fails, so it is not used as text on the hover surface. The moodboard's sampled secondary #505E6E gives 6.52:1 on #FDFDFD and is also safe.

lf-border-elevation.text: Default card: a 1 px hairline border with no shadow at rest; the hairline separates the tiles. The compact moodboard cards read as a catalogue with hairlines and no elevation. Elevation is one option among others (lf-elevation-options).

lf-radius.text: Default card and controls: card corners 8 px, control corners 6 px. The 999 px pill applies only to a count badge or to the stepper option (cc-add-steps), where the shadcn compact block grows its add control into a pill (scraped from s-shadcn-compact-card). Larger radii read as soft and playful; they stay one option among others.

lf-type-name.text: Product name at 15 px, weight 500, line height 1.35, one line with ellipsis. It stays lighter and smaller than the price, so the price is the strongest type in the tile (lf-card-anatomy, moodboard).

lf-type-meta.text: Meta line (material, size, count, stock) at 13 px, weight 400, line height 1.4, in the muted colour role. Stars with a bracketed count use this size too, so they do not compete with the price for weight.

lf-color-border.text: Two border roles. The decorative hairline #D9DCE1 gives only 1.37:1 on #FFFFFF, so it separates tiles and is not used alone as the edge of a control. A control edge (the add button outline, a stepper, a variant button) uses #8A909C, which gives 3.21:1 and meets the 3:1 non-text minimum of WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11. Where a control has a fill or a label, the edge is optional.
never_implies: a visible boundary for every control

lf-spacing-card-inset.text: Card inner padding of 12 px on a 140 to 148 px wide tile. At 12 px the text column keeps about 116 to 124 px for the name, which fits one line for most short product names and leaves room for the 48 px add target inside the card.

feel._about: Bindings, invariant and detectable signals: what 'compact', 'minimal' and 'modern' attach to, and what they must not leak into. Inferred from the exemplars and the research; these are reading aids, not requirements.

lf-bind-compact.text: 'Compact' binds to footprint: a tile about 140 to 148 px wide, so four fit across a 640 px frame with 16 px gutters (4 x 148 + 3 x 16 = 640). A wider tile fits fewer columns: three across at about 200 px is an option (compact_card/options/opt-three-across). It binds to size on the page, not to information density; a compact card can still be roomy inside.
never_implies: dense text or many small labels
tight tap targets (24 px floor; 48 px on touch)

lf-inv-one-action.invariant: each card carries one primary add action, and it is the strongest control on the card
lf-inv-one-action.variable: picture crop, presence of the meta line, presence of stars or a sale pill, the add label wording within 'Add to bag' / 'Add to cart' / 'Add'
lf-inv-one-action.scope: the default card in a grid
lf-inv-one-action.text: Default card reading only: each card carries one primary add action, the strongest control on the card. The variable is everything else the card shows. Check, when the filled option is chosen: exactly one filled control per card; secondary actions (details, wishlist, compare) are outlined or text. Other readings may carry a second primary action.

lf-signal-contrast.signal: every text role in the card meets 4.5:1 against its surface and every control edge meets 3:1; no meta or old-price text uses #9AA3B0 or lighter on white
lf-signal-contrast.text: A detectable check for a review pass: compute the ratio for each text colour against its surface (text 17.40:1; muted and old price 5.98:1 on white and 5.48:1 on #F5F5F5) and each control edge (#8A909C 3.21:1). Fail the review if #9AA3B0 or #6B7280 on #F5F5F5 appears as text.

lf-bind-minimal.text: 'Minimal' binds to how many parts a card shows by default: the listed parts (picture, name, meta line, price, add control). A star rating or a sale pill is an optional extra, shown only when it earns its place, and each one adds a row. Savings, details and benefits appear on request (a pill, a disclosure or a selector). It binds to count, not to the tone of the type or colour.

lf-bind-modern.text: 'Modern' binds to current conventions: flat hairline surfaces, one accent used for the action, a single system-style sans, and visible state changes instead of decoration. The research (Jakob's law, 20-research-primer) says modern should not cost recognition, so the add control and price keep the conventional places.

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices where the prompt and the evidence are silent

lf-elevation-options.text: Three options. (a) None: change the border or the surface only (#F5F5F5). (b) A hover surface change plus a faint lift, 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.06), on the card. (c) A focus ring only, 2 px in the accent with 2 px offset, no lift. Pick one and keep it for every card; a lift on hover alone is invisible to touch and keyboard users (see the hover-only reveal note in 21-research-specific).

lf-accent-options.text: Three options. (a) No accent: the add control is dark ink on white, filled in ink or outlined in ink, with the focus ring in ink. (b) One accent #1F4FD1 for the add control and focus ring, filled or outlined (dp-accent-fill; 6.78:1 with a white label). (c) The brand's own action colour, checked with the same ratio formula before use. The research supports (b) or (c); (a) suits a catalogue with no brand colour yet.

lf-price-rating-line.text: Price is the strongest type in the tile. Stars with a bracketed count sit under the name and above the price, small enough that they never compete with the price for weight. In the Cottonwick sale the price sits beside a small pill badge reading -25%, and the line beneath states the sale end date and days left.

lf-savings-modes.text: A three-segment toggle (Percent, Amount, Was and now) above the sale grid lets the shopper choose how the saving reads. The selected segment is the only filled control in that row; the others are outlined. Each tile shows the discount as a small pill next to the price and an end date in one muted line.

lf-details-disclosure.text: Details is a small disclosure button in the same row as Add to bag, so secondary information is one tap away without leaving the card. Opened, it shows a two-column spec list with muted small labels above values (Size, Material, Drainage, Care) and a one-line fit note. Progressive disclosure keeps the closed card short while the buy action stays visible.

lf-product-stage.term: product page stage and buy box
lf-product-stage.text: Three regions: a narrow vertical thumbnail rail on the left, a large stage in the middle, and a right-hand buy box about a third of the width. The buy box stacks category, name, a short description, finish swatches as labelled pills, a spec table (price, sizes, stock) separated by hairlines, then one full-width primary button. The only saturated colour on the page is that button; the stock line is plain text with the delivery date.

lf-benefit-selector.text: Three equal cells below the product name act as a segmented selector; the active cell has a lighter fill and a thin border. Selecting one swaps a horizontal bar comparison (this product against a typical one) with the value at the end of each bar. A pattern for showing one fact at a time instead of a spec wall.

lf-dark-palette.text: Photo-sampled values from the dark exemplars: page field near black (#0A0A0A to #0F0F0D), panel one step lighter (#1A1A1A), placeholder illustrations in mid-grey (#60615C to #61625D) with darker shadows (#393A35), and primary text near white (#FAFAFA). The image placeholders carry most of the colour, so the chrome can stay nearly monochrome. These are pixel samples of screenshots, not brand specs.

lf-light-palette.text: Photo-sampled values from the light exemplars: page white (#FDFDFD to #FEFEFE), a faint grey panel (#E6E7E8 to #E8E7EC), a deep navy for headings (#000E33) and a slate for secondary text (#505E6E). The Telerik schematic uses a pale blue frame (#F3F7FB) with pale placeholder tiles, and its strike-through prices sit in a very light blue-grey that is low contrast on white; a shop card should not copy that tint for the old price.

lf-state-strip.term: button state strip in a guide
lf-state-strip.text: A guide page lays one button out in its states side by side (default, hover, pressed, focus, disabled), with the difference carried by fill and label colour rather than size. Useful as a reference for reviewing the add control's states together.

lf-template-density.text: The Telerik template shows a tall card at reduced zoom: a red sale tag in the top-left corner, the title, a row of four small meta icons with values, and an avatar with a name and time. It is busier than the compact tile seen elsewhere, a counter-example: each extra meta row pushes the price and button further down the card.

lf-logos-not-evidence.term: logos and icons on reference pages
lf-logos-not-evidence.text: Eleven SVG files from the Telerik page (framework logos, the Progress wordmark and social icons) were viewed in the moodboard render. They are brand marks with no design information for a shopping component, so they are not evidence for tokens. Listed so the collection is accounted for.

lf-card-anatomy.text: Default card stack, top to bottom: the image, roughly square and filling the tile width; the name on one line; an optional muted meta line (material, size or capacity); the price, larger and heavier than the name; then the add control. Star rating is off in the default card (an-parts-optional). Placement and fill of the add control are options (anatomy/options/add_placement, anatomy/decision_points/dp-accent-fill); the one firm rule is a visible label at rest (inv-add-label). Tiles about 140 to 148 px wide with 16 px gutters fit four across a 640 px frame, which keeps the grid a catalogue rather than a poster.

lf-transfer.term: what transfers to a compact minimal card
lf-transfer.text: Across the exemplars the compact pattern keeps one image, one name, one muted meta line, a price, optional stars with count, and one add control whose placement is an option (anatomy/options/add_placement). Savings, details and benefits appear only on request (a pill, a disclosure, a selector). Dark stages use near-black fields with grey image placeholders and one saturated action. Light references need a stronger tint for the old price than the one they used.

anatomy._about: Anatomy of a compact shopping component: the parts and their order (researched from the compact card, the Telerik product-card guide and the moodboard exemplars), the readings of 'shopping component' (OPTIONS, not requirements: each is one plausible scope with what it includes; the default is marked, consumers choose or combine), the layout options (image-first is researched; text-first and row are OPTIONS), and the DECISION POINTS (choices the work will face, with what each option fits). Nothing here is decided for the user; the dump does not answer a decision point unless the user did.

readings._about: OPTIONS: each reading of 'shopping component' with what it includes. The default is marked. Synthesis writes these into essence.readings.

an-read-card.term: product card with add to cart
an-read-card.reading: product card with add to cart
an-read-card.text: Default reading: one product as a card in a list or grid, with an image, a name, a price and one add control. The card links to the product page and its quick add lets a shopper buy without opening that page.

an-read-buybox.term: buy box on a product page
an-read-buybox.reading: buy box on a product page
an-read-buybox.text: Option: the purchase panel beside the product image on a product page. It stacks the name, a short description, variant choices as labelled buttons, a spec or stock table, then one primary button. It fits when variant, stock or delivery detail needs to be read before adding.

an-read-minicart.text: Option: a small panel or drawer that lists what is in the bag, lets the shopper change quantity or remove an item, shows the subtotal and leads to checkout. It is the confirmation step that a quick add often opens.

an-read-list.text: Option: a grid or list of product cards with filters, a sort control and a result count. The card is one repeated unit inside it, so the card's parts and order carry over unchanged.

an-read-checkout.text: Option: the order summary beside or above the payment form. It lists the items, the subtotal, shipping, tax and the total, and ends in one place-order button. Prices here should match the card and cart exactly.

options._about: OPTIONS, not requirements: builder choices where the research is silent. Proposed, tier 2 at most.

add_placement._about: options, not requirements: placement of the add control. The one firm rule is a visible label at rest (inv-add-label).

an-opt-add-full-width.text: Placement option A: a full-width labelled button below the price, with a plus icon beside the label (for example Add to bag). The moodboard exemplars use this placement (lf-card-anatomy). It fits a card whose main action is the add. One option among others.

an-opt-add-corner-plus.text: Placement option B: a round plus on the picture corner (the compact demo, cc-parts-order), with a visible short label beside it at rest (for example Add), so the rest state is not icon-only. It fits a dense grid of small goods where the image leads. One option among others.

cc-add-reveal.term: add control reveal on hover and focus

heading_path: Compact Product Card Block for React
The plus is hidden until hover. What about phones?

cc-add-reveal.text: Option B with a reveal: on a desktop the plus appears when the tile is hovered or when anything inside it has keyboard focus, so tabbing to a tile shows its control; on touch screens the plus stays visible. Under inv-add-label the rest state keeps a visible label, so this reveal can only add emphasis to a control that is already labelled; a label-free reveal is not an option here. A tile with something in the bag keeps its stepper showing. One option among others.
cc-add-reveal.quote: On a desktop it reveals on hover and as soon as anything in the tile has keyboard focus

an-opt-text-first.text: Option: name and price above a smaller image, so the words lead and the image supports. Fits when attributes decide the purchase; the layout is untested against the exemplars.

an-opt-row.text: Option: a horizontal card with the image on the left and name, price and add control stacked on the right. Fits lists that are read as rows (carts, search results, small goods); it needs a fixed image width so the text column lines up.

decision_points._about: Decision points: each choice the work will face, with options and what each fits. Options, not answers.

dp-accent-fill._about: options, not requirements: the fill of the add control when one accent is chosen

opt-accent-filled.text: Filled: the add control's fill is the accent #1F4FD1 with a #FFFFFF label (6.78:1). One option among others.

opt-accent-outlined.text: Outlined: no fill; the label and a 1 px edge are the accent #1F4FD1 on white (6.78:1 for both, which clears the 3:1 non-text minimum). Secondary actions stay outlined or text. One option among others.

dp-quick-add-vs-buybox.decision: quick add on the card or a buy box on a product page

options.fits_when: the product has one purchasable form, or shoppers compare many items in a grid

options.option: buy box on the product page
options.fits_when: variants, specs, stock or delivery needs to be read before adding

options.option: configuration-first tile: choose on the card, buy on a detail step
options.fits_when: the product is chosen by configuration and the card should carry no price-and-cart conflict

dp-quick-add-vs-buybox.text: Decision: whether the add action lives on the card, on a buy box, or is split between them.

options.option: image-led: the image is most of the tile, name and price stay small
options.fits_when: the look sells the product, as with apparel, furniture, food or art

options.option: text-led: name, attributes and price lead, with a small image
options.fits_when: the product is chosen by its attributes, as with parts, electronics or dense lists

dp-image-vs-text-led.text: Decision: which element leads the card. Image-first (an-layout-image-first) is the researched default; text-led is the alternative when attributes decide.

dp-ratings.decision: show ratings on the card or not

options.option: show stars with count under the name
options.fits_when: reviews drive the choice and each product has enough reviews to read

options.option: hide ratings on the card; keep them on the product page
options.fits_when: the card stays minimal with one price and one action, or review counts are low and would read as a weak signal

dp-ratings.text: Decision: whether the card carries a rating row. Each row pushes the price and button down.

dp-quantity.decision: quantity on the card or only in the cart

options.option: stepper on the card: the add control grows into minus, count, plus
options.fits_when: shoppers buy several of the same item in one visit, as with small goods or consumables

options.option: single add on the card; quantity in the mini cart or cart
options.fits_when: one of each is typical, and the card stays a single action

dp-quantity.text: Decision: whether the card holds a quantity stepper. The compact demo replaces the plus with a stepper after the first add.

options.fits_when: the card context makes the action obvious and space is tight

options.option: Add to bag or Add to cart
options.fits_when: the shop's own word for its cart is the one shoppers already use
the card-level action needs telling apart from a buy box on the product page

dp-button-wording.text: Decision: the add label. Its states can run Add, Adding, Added; 'Added to cart' can read as a link to checkout, so pair the added state with a count badge or a check mark, not the words alone.

options.option: no accent: type and greyscale images carry the card
options.fits_when: the product images already carry the colour

options.option: one accent on the primary add action
options.fits_when: the add action needs to be the clearest choice, as the moodboard buy box does

options.option: accent on the sale marker or price
options.fits_when: the price change is the message, as in a sale grid; it competes with the add action

dp-accent.text: Decision: one accent or none, and if one, where. Competing calls to action distract from the add action. The fill of the add control (filled or outlined) is an option in dp-accent-fill.

an-layers.text: Layers, so each property sits on one level and does not drift: the component (parts, their order, states, the add control), the page context (grid, filters, the surrounding list), the product data (name, price, variants, stock), the visual tokens (spacing, type, colour, radius), the motion (reveal, add feedback) and the evoked feeling (calm, product-first). A grid gap is page context, not a card property.

an-variants-null.text: Variant fields a shopper picks before adding: size, finish or colour, and quantity. Each value is a field of the product data. Null rule: a missing value is unknown and is shown as unknown (for example 'stock not listed'), not filled in from a sibling variant. A size with no stock figure does not borrow the count of another size.

inv-add-label.invariant: the add control shows a visible text label at rest
inv-add-label.variable: shape, fill, placement, icon and reveal of the add control (anatomy/options/add_placement, dp-accent-fill)
inv-add-label.text: The one firm rule for the add control: a visible text label at rest that names the action (for example Add to bag), with an accessible name that also names the product. Shape, fill, placement and reveal are options. A round plus alone is icon-only and does not meet the rule.

inv-card-order.invariant: the shopper reads the product (image and name) and its price before the add control
inv-card-order.variable: image ratio and crop, the meta line, the rating, swatches, the add control's placement (below the price or on the image corner) and its wording
inv-card-order.scope: the default product card and its variants
inv-card-order.text: On the default card, the product comes first and the action last; everything else in the card can change. Other readings may place the action differently.

an-parts-order.text: Parts of the default card, top to bottom: the image (near-square, filling the tile width), the name on one line (the name is the link to the product page), an optional muted meta line (material, size or capacity), the price as the strongest type, then the add control. The placement of the add control is an option (anatomy/options/add_placement); the one firm rule is a visible label at rest (inv-add-label). The order of image, name and price holds in every placement.

an-parts-optional.text: Parts that appear only when they earn their place, and none of them is in the default card: star rating with count (under the name, above the price), a sale marker (a small pill beside the price, with the former price struck through), colour or finish swatches (a count such as '+3 more' under the name), a stock or delivery line, a quantity stepper (cc-add-steps). Each one adds a row and pushes the price and button down. The default card lists picture, name, meta line (optional), price and the add control.

an-layout-image-first.text: Default card layout: a vertical card with the image on top and the text and price stacked below. Both Telerik demo cards use it; the page does not describe the layout in words, so this reading comes from the screenshot. It suits grids where each tile needs to read on its own. A horizontal row is one option among others (an-opt-row).

states._about: The states one add-to-cart control passes through, what changes in each, the feedback and timing around them, motion, and keyboard and screen-reader behavior. Researched values come from fetched pages (UXPin button states, NN/g, the shadcn compact card, Nicole Chan's accessible add-to-cart talk, WCAG, Baymard). Values the sources do not give (add-feedback ms, transition ms, the low-stock threshold) are options or open questions, not facts.
Visible states of one add control, in the order a shopper meets them.

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices where the sources are silent

opt-low-stock-n.when: stock is at or below a threshold N
opt-low-stock-n.then: show the remaining count as text beside the control
opt-low-stock-n.text: Option only. The fetched sources give no threshold N, so N is an open question (q-low-stock-n). A text cue reads without colour and sits where the out-of-stock reason sits.

st-loading.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
then: the label stays in place and a spinner sits beside it (UXPin suggests a spinner in place of or beside the text)
the control is disabled while the request runs (UXPin)
st-loading.text: One option among others, and conditional: a loading state applies only where an add request is pending (a server-backed cart). Where it applies, the label stays in place with a spinner beside it, the control is disabled while the request runs, and the change is announced politely. A card whose add is local state (cc-feedback-status) has no pending request, so it needs no loading state.

st-disabled.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
st-disabled.when: the product is out of stock or a required option is not selected
then: the control stays visible at reduced opacity or a muted palette (UXPin)
a line of text beside the control says why it is unavailable (UXPin: explain where possible)
the markup carries either the disabled attribute or aria-disabled; the choice is open (see the text)
st-disabled.text: A disabled add control is visible and explained, not only grey. Disabled attribute versus aria-disabled is open: the disabled attribute can drop keyboard focus unless focus is managed, while aria-disabled keeps focus but may be announced as unavailable in a way that reads ambiguously in shopping. Nicole Chan's talk recommends user testing to choose between them, and asks that the label, the attribute and the stock check agree.

st-added.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
st-added.when: at least one piece of the product is in the bag
then: the single round plus becomes a pill with minus, the count and plus
minus at one takes the piece back and the pill returns to a single plus
any colour change carries a second cue such as a checkmark or text, and the text keeps 4.5:1 in pressed and disabled (UXPin)
a demo caps the count at nine; the cap is that demo's choice, not a rule
st-added.text: Added changes the control from an action into a count. The count replaces the plus, so the stepper does not open a panel. Nicole Chan notes that Added to Cart can read as a link to checkout, so pair the label with a count badge or a checkmark as well as a colour change.

inv-add-control.invariant: the add control keeps a text cue or a count, and a visible edge, in every state
inv-add-control.variable: fill colour, icon, padding, single plus versus pill, and the space around the control
inv-add-control.scope: default, hover, pressed, focus-visible, disabled, loading, added
inv-add-control.text: Across the states, the cue that the control adds stays readable without colour, and the state can be read with colour removed. What varies is the look, not the cue.

st-default.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
st-default.when: no piece is in the bag and the product is in stock
st-default.text: Default shows the labelled add control. Its pointer target is at least 24 by 24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8 floor). On touch it is at least 48 by 48 px (Material's 48 dp), with 8 px or more between targets; 44 by 44 pt (Apple) is an option and the floor for a tight layout. The focus-visible ring is at least a 2 CSS px perimeter at 3:1 against the surface (WCAG 2.4.13 is AAA; 1.4.11 sets the 3:1). Text on the control keeps 4.5:1 in every state. The label wording is a choice (q-add-label).
