st-state-set.rung: product cards, carts and quick add

heading_path: Button States Explained: The Complete Design Guide for 2026

st-state-set.text: The UXPin guide lists seven button states: default, hover, active (pressed), focus, disabled, loading and toggle, and says most buttons need four to seven. For an add-to-cart control the working set is default, hover, pressed, focus-visible and disabled; loading is a conditional option (st-loading), and toggle applies only when the control switches between two conditions, such as added and not added.

st-hover-pressed.rung: product cards, carts and quick add

heading_path: Button States Explained: The Complete Design Guide for 2026

st-hover-pressed.text: Hover: a subtle change such as a slight colour shift, an elevation shadow or an underline, noticeable but not jarring, with no dramatic animation. Pressed: darkening, an inset shadow or a small scale reduction, applied between mousedown and mouseup and reversed cleanly on release. The page gives no duration for either. Pressed and hover feedback should appear at or under 100 ms (NN/g response limit); 80 to 100 ms are the options (opt-motion-durations). Hover does not exist on touch screens, so information that appears only on hover is out of reach there. For add-to-cart, pressed is the first acknowledgement, before the request or cart update returns.

feedback._about: What the shopper sees after and around an add, and how long the sources say it should last.

options._about: options, not requirements: none of these values are sourced in ms

opt-feedback-duration.text: Options for how long the add confirmation stays: (a) persist until the shopper acts or moves on, with a link to the cart; (b) a timed dismissal, duration unsourced, to test over a range such as 3000 to 5000 ms; (c) no overlay, only the count and the status line. The fetched sources give no millisecond value for the add confirmation (q-confirm-ms).

opt-error-presentation.text: Options for a failed add: (a) an inline text message beside the control, with the label back to Add; (b) the same message in the polite status region, so it is announced; (c) focus moved to the message. No fetched source covers the error state, so the choice is open.

fb-persistent.rung: product cards, carts and quick add
fb-persistent.text: NN/g advises against overlays that fade away quickly: a fashion retailer's add overlay confirmed the addition but vanished fast, so shoppers could not check what they had added. Baymard describes an Added to Cart overlay as a highly effective confirmation. Neither source gives a duration in milliseconds, so the duration is an open question (q-confirm-ms).

fb-status-count.rung: product cards, carts and quick add

heading_path: Compact Product Card Block for React

fb-status-count.text: The bag count in the heading row adds up every piece in the bag. A polite status line announces what changed. Nothing is stored, charged or sent, and motion is limited to CSS for the reveal and entrance. A compact card can keep its running total in the heading row and announce changes through a status region instead of a modal.

motion._about: Timing and motion for state changes. The sourced values are response-time limits, not transition durations.

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices with no source in ms

opt-motion-durations.text: Options, unsourced: (a) hover and pressed colour transitions at 80 to 100 ms with ease-out, so pressed feedback stays at or under the 100 ms response limit (sp-response-limits); (b) the round plus or label reveal on hover or focus at 80 to 100 ms as well, so hover feedback stays within the limit; (c) reduced motion: keep the colour, text and count changes and drop the movement, using a prefers-reduced-motion media query (inferred from standard CSS practice; no fetched source covers reduced motion). Open questions q-motion-ms and q-reduced-motion.

values.feel: directly manipulating objects in the UI
about the limit for keeping attention on the dialogue

mo-response-limits.text: NN/g's response-time limits are about 0.1 s for direct manipulation, about 1 s for free navigation, and about 10 s for keeping attention. Applied to the add control (inferred from these limits): pressed feedback inside about 0.1 s, and a visible loading or added state for any request that takes longer than about 1 s.

fs-motion-duration.from: a longer or faster motion duration
fs-motion-duration.why: the response limits above set the perceptual windows; whether a state reads depends on the cue (text, icon, count or colour), not on how long a motion lasts

access._about: Name, role, keyboard and announcement behavior of the add control.

heading_path: Compact Product Card Block for React

ac-name.text: Each button names its product, for example 'Add [product] to the bag' or 'One fewer [product]'. The control is a native button element (inferred: the page names each button, it does not state the element). The wording cart or bag is a choice; the draft's lexicon keeps both.

ac-live-region.text: Accessible add-to-cart flows announce cart changes through a live region that already exists in the DOM when the page loads, with aria-live set to polite or assertive, and the script updates its text. Notifications that hold interactive content work better when focus moves to them than with a live region alone.

heading_path: Compact Product Card Block for React

ac-keyboard-focus.text: Where the reveal option applies (cc-add-reveal, anatomy/options/add_placement), on desktop the round plus appears on hover or when anything inside the tile has keyboard focus, so tabbing to a tile shows its control; on touch screens the plus stays visible. The one firm rule still holds: the rest state keeps a visible label. When minus removes the last piece (the stepper option), focus returns to the add control, so a keyboard user keeps their place. Everything in the component works from the keyboard, per the page.

lexicon._about: The brain-dump pass for a compact, minimal, modern shopping component: how people talk about the feel, the moods and metaphors around it, the meant sense of each ambiguous word, and candidate search vocabulary. Tier 3-4 seed material, inferred from common design practice and not fetched; it widens the work and defines nothing.

associations._about: Human descriptors, moods, metaphors, adjacent practices and influences around the key qualities and the object. Inferred; no fetched source backs these.

senses._about: The meant sense of each ambiguous prompt word. The excluded senses are the matching not_meant anti-keywords (ak-component-hardware, ak-shopping-hobby, ak-compact-dense, ak-minimal-empty, ak-modern-trendy).

lx-sense-component.text: A UI component: a reusable interface unit with markup, states and behavior, such as a product card or a buy box. Not a hardware part.

lx-sense-shopping.text: The purchase flow: from a product in a list to adding it to the bag. Not window shopping as leisure, and not a shopping hobby.

lx-sense-compact.text: A small footprint for the same job: few parts, short distances and ordered, tight spacing. Not dense information, which packs many data points into one view.

lx-sense-minimal.text: The fewest elements that still work, each one needed and finished. Not empty or unfinished, which drops parts a shopper needs.

lx-sense-modern.text: Current interface conventions: clear type, honest color, familiar controls and visible states. Not trendy effects such as neon glows or glassmorphism.

search_vocabulary._about: Candidate vocabulary: search phrases, titles and alt text drafted for this component. Candidates to test and pick from before use.

lx-sv-short-card.text: Short search phrase: compact product card.

lx-sv-short-add.text: Short search phrase: minimal add to cart button.

lx-sv-medium-quick-add.term: minimal product card with quick add
lx-sv-medium-quick-add.text: Medium search phrase: minimal product card with quick add.

lx-sv-medium-modern.term: modern shopping component for product cards
lx-sv-medium-modern.text: Medium search phrase: modern shopping component for product cards.

lx-sv-long-stepper.term: compact product card with add to bag button and quantity stepper
lx-sv-long-stepper.text: Long-tail search phrase: compact product card with add to bag button and quantity stepper.

lx-sv-title.term: compact product card with quick add
lx-sv-title.text: Natural page or block title: Compact product card with quick add.

lx-sv-alt.text: Alt text template: Product photo of [item] on a plain light background, shown at card size.

lx-assoc-shopping-mood.text: How a buy action tends to feel: decisive, reassuring and unhurried. Contributes the tone of the add label, a calm confirmation and a control that does not push urgency. Copy descriptors: clear, settled, easy.

lx-assoc-price-tag.text: A price tag on a shelf or a hang tag on a folded garment: the card as a displayed object with its price on a small plate. Contributes the price as a short, separate label with its currency and unit, and the image as the item being shown.

lx-assoc-bag-vocabulary.text: The container words shoppers use for the cart: bag reads lighter and more current in many shops, cart reads functional, basket is the common UK word. Contributes the wording of the add control and the count in the heading.

lx-assoc-compact-snug.text: Descriptors for compact: snug, pocket-sized, tidy, contained, close-packed but calm. Sensory: a small footprint, short distances, a tight grip. Contributes short internal spacing, a limited number of parts and a small image ratio.

lx-assoc-compact-bento.text: A bento box or a pocket notebook: many things kept in one small frame, each in its own compartment with exact sizes. Contributes a grid of fixed cells with visible dividers, so a compact card reads as organized space, not crowded text.

lx-assoc-minimal-quiet.text: Descriptors for minimal: quiet, airy, uncluttered, restrained, edited, plain. Sensory: a pale surface, open margins, one clear line of type. Contributes fewer parts, one accent or none, and generous space inside the frame.

lx-assoc-minimal-influence.text: Influences: the less-but-better product-design tradition associated with Dieter Rams, and the plain catalogue look of Muji. Contributes restraint and utility: each element earns its place and the product leads. An influence to draw on, not a style to copy.

lx-assoc-modern-current.text: Descriptors for modern: current, crisp, contemporary, fresh, up to date. Sensory: clean edges, an even rhythm, a sans-serif voice. Contributes current conventions (one sans family, corners set once, dark mode support) rather than decorative effects.

lx-assoc-modern-practice.text: Design systems, tokens, responsive layout, dark mode and reduced-motion support: the practices that make an interface read as current. Contributes the token-driven spacing, color roles and motion settings used in the other sections.

lx-assoc-modern-caption.text: A gallery wall label: small, precise type, plenty of air, a single caption line. Contributes a modern feel built on quiet hierarchy and a small, exact meta line.

exclusion._about: Forbidden shortcuts: invalid inferences a model tends to make about a compact, minimal, modern shopping component. Each is a constraint on reasoning, not a style rule.

ex-smaller-accessible.text: A smaller component is not automatically more accessible. Shrinking the text, the target or the contrast to fit more on screen lowers access. Compact comes from fewer parts and tighter spacing, with target sizes, contrast and text size held at their minimums.
ex-smaller-accessible.never_implies: that shrinking any dimension is an accessibility fix

ex-minimal-is-missing.text: Minimal is not missing. Removing the price, the name or the add control leaves a broken component. Minimal removes decoration and optional parts, not the information needed to buy.
ex-minimal-is-missing.never_implies: that dropping a required part makes a component more minimal

ex-color-only-state.text: Color alone does not signal added, sold out or error. Pair each state color with a text label or an icon, because a color change alone fails for color-blind users and is invisible to screen readers.
